title: Ground Veal Ragù for Lasagna
cScaleSummary: Approximately 21–24 mg cholesterol per serving, primarily from the ground veal, with smaller contributions from the Parmesan and chicken stock.
ldlActiveSummary: The ragù is low in fiber and centered on veal and Parmesan. Its vegetables and olive oil are beneficial but insufficient to make it actively LDL-lowering.
intro: Ground-meat ragù appears throughout Italy in countless regional forms, ranging from restrained northern sauces to more tomato-forward preparations associated with southern Italian and Italian-American cooking. This version uses ground veal for delicate richness, while fresh thyme, sage, rosemary and nutmeg create a quieter, more herbaceous character than conventional red sauce. A small amount of fish sauce strengthens the savory foundation without announcing itself. Parmesan deepens the finish, and fresh parsley provides brightness. Cooked until exceptionally thick, this ragù is designed for layering without making the finished lasagna watery. It yields about 5 cups.

items.item: kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper

stepGroups.title: Brown the Veal
items: Heat {{ingredient:olive-oil}} in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Brown the veal in two batches, breaking it into small but distinct pieces. Allow each batch to develop deeply browned edges before stirring. Transfer the browned veal to a bowl.

stepGroups.title: Build the Aromatic Base
items: Reduce the heat to medium. Add {{ingredient:yellow-onion}}, {{ingredient:carrot}}, and {{ingredient:aromatic-salt}}. Cook for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables are very soft and beginning to brown.
Add {{ingredient:garlic}}, {{ingredient:thyme}}, {{ingredient:sage}}, and {{ingredient:rosemary}} and cook for 30 seconds.

stepGroups.title: Develop the Flavor Backbone
items: Add {{ingredient:tomato-paste}}, {{ingredient:red-pepper-flakes}}, and {{ingredient:nutmeg}}. Cook for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring frequently, until the tomato paste turns dark brick red and begins sticking to the bottom of the pot.
Add {{ingredient:red-wine}}, scrape up the browned residue, and simmer until the wine has reduced by approximately three-quarters.

stepGroups.title: Simmer the Ragù
items: Return the veal and its accumulated juices to the pot. Add {{ingredient:whole-peeled-tomatoes}}, {{ingredient:chicken-stock}}, {{ingredient:fish-sauce}}, and {{ingredient:bay-leaf}}, then bring the mixture just to a simmer.
Reduce the heat to low and cook uncovered for 75 to 90 minutes, stirring occasionally. Stir more frequently during the final 30 minutes as the ragù thickens.

stepGroups.title: Finish the Ragù
items: Remove the bay leaf. Stir in {{ingredient:parmesan}} and {{ingredient:parsley}}.
Taste and adjust the seasoning. Continue cooking until the ragù is considerably thicker than an ordinary pasta sauce.
Drag a spoon across the bottom of the pot. The track should remain visible for several seconds, with no watery tomato liquid collecting around the meat. Cool before assembling the lasagna.
